name: What if the detached ADU needs fire access or driveway changes?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a detached ADU design requires driveway changes, fire access clearance, or a new side path?
mainEntity.text: What happens if a detached ADU design requires driveway changes, fire access clearance, or a new side path?

acceptedAnswer.text: Access is one of the most underestimated parts of detached ADU planning. A unit that looks workable on paper can become difficult if the site lacks a clear construction path, fire access, or enough room for equipment and material movement. Driveway changes, side-yard access improvements, and gate relocations can all add cost and affect the final layout. In some cases, the ADU must be shifted, reduced, or redesigned to preserve required access routes. Homeowners should ask the design team to study how workers, inspections, trash removal, and future occupant access will function before finalizing the floor plan. This matters especially on narrow lots and rear-yard builds. A practical site plan should show not only the ADU itself, but also how people and materials move around it. Solving access early is much cheaper than fixing it after the permit review starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Driveway and fire access issues can change the entire site plan. If access is too narrow or blocked, the design may need a revised layout, added hardscape, or reconfigured circulation to satisfy local review and construction needs.
